skipped_jobs: Fast check (non-engine code path, R399 W4)

root_cause.evidence: check-run annotation: 'The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased. Please check the Billing & plans section in your settings.'
root_cause.diagnosis: No GitHub-hosted runner was assigned to the classify job; the job never started. This is an account-level billing/limit issue, not a code defect. The workflow YAML is valid; the dorny/paths-filter step is syntactically correct. The failure occurs at runner allocation, before any step executes.
root_cause.operator_action_required: Resolve the GitHub account billing issue (check Billing & plans in GitHub settings; increase spending limit or add a payment method). Once runners can be allocated, the classify job will run and the downstream certify/fast-check jobs will execute.

local_reproduction.note: The classify step's path-filter logic was reproduced locally: the dorny/paths-filter@v3 action is a deterministic path matcher. On the R548 push (engine-relevant files: discovery_fabric/engine/adapters.py, mechanism_space.py, toscanini/server.py), engine_paths=true, so the certify job SHOULD run (the 14-gate certification). The failure is purely at the runner-assignment layer.

recent_runs_all_failure.note: The R538 diagnosis (R538/R538_CI_DIAGNOSIS.json) confirmed 100/100 recent runs all failure with zero-step runner assignment. This is a standing infrastructure blocker, not a regression introduced by R548.

what_unblocks: GitHub account billing resolution (spending limit / payment method). No code change can fix a runner-allocation failure.
